title: EXAMPLE SET — FAKE, PUBLIC, NOT A QUALITY SIGNAL
warning: This set is committed to a PUBLIC repository on purpose, so the schema is documentable and
scripts/eval_private_selftest.sh has something real to run against. Every item below is
invented nonsense. It is contaminated by construction the moment it is pushed.
It has 3 live items, which is below AHL_PRIVATE_MIN_ITEMS=30, so a run against it can never
produce a citable row: it records `small_n` and status=suspect. That is deliberate --
the example cannot be mistaken for the gate.
"visibility": "example" is NOT what makes this set public. Being THIS path with THESE
bytes is. eval_private_set.py pins the sha256 of both files; edit either one and the set
becomes private -- the runner refuses to run it from inside the repo, the pre-commit guard
blocks it, and this published salt is rejected by value. Copying this directory therefore
does not copy its exemption, which is the whole point: the copy is the thing an operator
The real set lives OUTSIDE this repo and is created with `scripts/eval_private.sh init`,
which generates a fresh random salt. See docs/private-eval.md.
authoring_notes: Fields consumed by the runner: schema, set_id, visibility, salt, champion. Everything else (title, warning, authored, authoring_notes) is for humans. A real set's `salt` must be >=32 random characters generated once and never published -- it is what stops the audit digests in results/**/data/ from being a confirmation oracle for guessed questions. `champion` records which model's verdicts calibrated the items, so a later failure can be attributed to the candidate rather than to a wrong answer key; it is required for every set except this one.
